text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States says Albania's October local polls were sufficiently fair but called on the government to pass a new constitution and hold fresh general elections.
- The government is preparing a draft law aimed at supporting tobacco cultivation and curbing cigarette smuggling.
- A mission of the International Monetary Fund is expected to visit Albania this month.
- The director of the Albanian American Enterprise Fund says it is up to the government to decide on the future of suspected pyramid schemes and only additional investment could save such companies.
- A group of young Socialists have asked their leader Ilir Meta to resign from the party and politics after he called for the party's leadership to quit following a poor showing in local elections.
- Corruption has engulfed hospitals in the capital Tirana.
- Italian Ambassador Paolo Foresti says Italian observers noticed serious irregularities during local elections on October but said conduct elsewhre in the country had been far better.
- Rightist parties are considering forming a broader alliance after a coalition of two of them managed to win the Shkodra municipality in October's local polls.
- Albania's Silva company, which exploits bitumen sands deposits, acquired machines and equipment worth $2 million from Italy's Maia Caterpillar.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha congratulates German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on his record term in office.
